description.narrative: Isiolo County is facing a growing water crisis driven by increasing climate variability in Kenya’s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs). The county experiences both prolonged droughts and recurrent flooding, which together strain water resources, livelihoods, and ecosystems. Extended dry periods have reduced flows in the Ewaso Ng’iro River, lowered groundwater levels, and degraded wetlands that support communities, livestock, and pastoralist livelihoods. Conversely, intense rainfall events trigger flash floods that erode riverbanks, damage water infrastructure, and disrupt settlements along the Lower Ewaso Ng’iro River. Flood risks are particularly acute in Merti, Gafarsa, Malka Daka, Iresaboru, Badana, and Sericho. These risks are exacerbated by the widespread invasion of Prosopis juliflora (Mathenge) in floodplains, which obstructs river channels, alters flow paths, and increases flood intensity during the rainy season while reducing water availability during dry periods. In addition, shifts in the river’s meandering channel have left some settlements without reliable and direct access to water in dry seasons.The objective of this short-term remote assignment (two working days) is to provide rapid analytical support to the Dutch Disaster Risk Reduction & Surge Support (DRRS) team in preparation for a one-week scoping deployment to Isiolo County, Kenya. The assignment will focus on a desk-based compilation and synthesis of key baseline information, drawing on readily available secondary data and geospatial datasets. The outputs will support an initial understanding of flood risk dynamics, water management considerations, and the prioritisation of field scoping activities during the in-country mission.
